podcast.title: Estrangement from Blink 182 (2005-2022)
podcast.body: Following Blink 182's indefinite hiatus in 2005, Tom DeLonge and Mark Hoppus did not communicate for years. He notably quit Blink 182 twice, the second time in early 2015, either to focus on non-musical projects or due to an unwillingness to sign a contract requiring sole focus on the band. He remained estranged from Mark and Travis through 2021. "Tom DeLong and bass player Mark Hoppiz did not talk for years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Catching Up with Blink 182

podcast.title: Focus on Non-Musical Projects (2015 onwards)
podcast.body: After his second departure from Blink 182 in 2015, Tom DeLonge explicitly stated his intention to focus his energies on non-musical projects. "He wanted to focus his energies on non-musical projects."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Catching Up with Blink 182

podcast.title: UFO Research and To The Stars Academy of Arts and Sciences (Post-2015)
podcast.body: Tom DeLonge developed a strong passion for UFO research, which became a central focus of his non-musical endeavors. He founded the company To the Stars Academy of Arts and Sciences and co-wrote books on the subject. "His new passion was UFO research, and his company to the stars Academy of Arts and Sciences, and the book C was co-writing on the subject, were his thing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Catching Up with Blink 182

podcast.title: Reconciliation with Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker (2022)
podcast.body: Upon learning of Mark Hoppus's cancer diagnosis, Tom DeLonge immediately reached out, leading to a crucial meeting in Mark's backyard that included Travis Barker. During this sit-down, they discussed life experiences, growth, and the realization that personal issues paled in comparison to Mark's health. This meeting was pivotal in healing damaged relationships and ultimately facilitated Tom's return to Blink 182. "When Tom's long heard about Mark, he was right there and soon there was a sit down in Mark's backyard."

podcast.title: "All the Small Things" Inspiration
podcast.body: He personally wrote the hit song "All the Small Things" for his then-girlfriend, Jennifer, with the specific intention of creating a catchy and commercially successful track. "All the small things, Tom DeLong wrote that for his girlfriend, Jennifer."

podcast.title: Childhood and Skater Identity
podcast.body: Growing up in the San Diego suburb of Poe, Tom DeLong was described as a solid C student and a "menace" on his skateboard, frequently chasing people off sidewalks throughout the city. "Tom DeLong is from the San Diego suburb of Poe. When he was a kid, a solid C student, he was a menace on his skateboard, chasing people off sidewalks from one end of the city to the other."

podcast.title: Devotion to UFO Research
podcast.body: Tom DeLonge is completely devoted to discovering the truth behind UFOs, a passion so strong that he quit Blink-182 to focus on this project. He founded "To The Stars Academy," a serious organization staffed with scientists, engineers, and military personnel, all dedicated to believing and investigating UFOs. "He is completely Devoted to discovering the truth behind UFOs and that's one of the reasons he quit the band to focus on this project as much as he can"

podcast.title: Entrepreneurial Ventures
podcast.body: Outside of music, Tom DeLonge founded a shoe company called McBeth, which achieved success. He also established a software company named Mod Life, specifically designed to help musicians monetize their creative output. These ventures reflected his diverse interests beyond performance. "Plus, he had a shoe company called McBeth that was doing well. Then there was his software company called Mod Life, which is aimed at helping musicians monetize what they produced."

podcast.title: Financial Security
podcast.body: Tom DeLonge possesses substantial financial resources, which contribute to his overall satisfaction and independence. Being part of a band that sold approximately 40 million albums means that monetary concerns are largely irrelevant for him. "He has more than enough money to keep him happy. And when you're in a band that sold 40 million or so albums, you know, money's not much of a problem."

podcast.title: Lost Time Periods Near Area 51
podcast.body: While researching Area 51, Tom DeLonge claims to have endured "lost time periods" during which he cannot remember what happened. This occurred when he was camping near Groom Lake in Nevada, where he had some kind of encounter, and next thing he knew, three hours had passed without his recollection. "He was camping out near Groom Lake in Nevada when he had some kind of encounter Next thing he knows three hours had gone by and he has no idea what happened during those three hours"

podcast.title: Personal Hardships (2000s)
podcast.body: During the mid-2000s, Tom DeLonge faced significant personal challenges. His brother was deployed to Iraq, a war he opposed, and his father was diagnosed with leukemia. These events, combined with the Blink-182 breakup and a serious back injury that led to painkiller addiction, created a difficult period in his life. "His brother was deployed to Iraq, a war that Tom opposed. His father was diagnosed with leukemia. In other words, it wasn't a very good time."

podcast.title: Political Activism
podcast.body: Tom DeLonge became actively involved in politics, endorsing John Kerry for president and campaigning on the election circuit for a period. His political engagement stemmed from a desire for reform after four years of George Bush's presidency, deeply influencing the philosophical underpinnings of his band, Angels & Airwaves. "He endorsed John Kerry for president. He got sucked into politics. He even toured the election circuit for a while."

xref.title: Indefinite Hiatus (2005)
xref.body: An indefinite hiatus was announced on February 22nd, 2005, following a period of uncertainty and internal friction, during which Tom DeLonge and Mark Hoppus ceased communication for years. "Things got to the point where they couldn't continue, and an indefinite hiatus was announced on February 22nd, 2005."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Catching Up with Blink 182

xref.title: Indefinite Hiatus and Breakup (2005)
xref.body: Over Christmas 2004, old tensions resurfaced, leading to a breakdown in communication among band members. On February 22, 2005, management announced an "indefinite hiatus." The statement explained the band's need for time with loved ones after over a decade of non-stop work. However, this was effectively a breakup, initiated when Tom DeLonge's demand for a six-month break was deemed too long by Mark and Travis, leading to Tom quitting the band. "On February 22, 2005, announcing that the group was going on, quote, indefinite hiatus."

xref.title: Resurfacing Internal Issues (Late 2014)
xref.body: After their album *Dogs Eating Dogs* and more tours, the "old cracks returned" within the band. Issues between Tom DeLonge and Mark Hoppus, coupled with Travis Barker's fear of flying preventing overseas tours, came to a head in late 2014. "There were more tours, but the old cracks returned."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Catching Up with Blink 182

xref.title: Tom DeLonge's Departures (2014-2015)
xref.body: Tom DeLonge initially quit the band for one day in early 2014 but was persuaded to return. Tensions escalated again in early 2015 when he insisted on recording his parts in San Diego while Mark and Travis worked in LA. A week before studio convergence, Mark and Travis received an email from Tom's manager stating his unwillingness to participate, citing a desire to focus on non-musical projects. Another account suggests he was presented with a 60-page contract demanding sole focus on Blink, which he couldn't accept due to prior commitments. He consequently quit for a second time. "Tensions built, and a week before everyone was supposed to convene in the studio for the final push, Mark and Travis got an email from Tom's manager saying that he no longer wanted to participate in Blink 182."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Catching Up with Blink 182

xref.title: Tom Delonge's Second Departure (2014-2015)
xref.body: Tom Delonge quit the band again around 2014, although he briefly returned proposing group therapy led by motivational speaker Tony Robbins, which did not resolve underlying issues. Communication ceased once more, leading to indefinite delays for a planned 2013 album. His manager eventually sent an email, one week before a scheduled studio session, stating Tom's indefinite unwillingness to participate in Blink-182 activities. The band issued a statement announcing his departure, to which Tom countered that the band demanded he put all other projects on hold for an album and tour within six months. He refused these terms and officially left. "Tom's manager sent an email... saying that Tom did not want to participate in any Blink activities indefinitely."

xref.title: Matt Skiba's Recruitment and First Performance (2015)
xref.body: After Tom DeLonge's second departure, Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker decided against disbanding Blink 182 and recruited Matt Skiba from Alkaline Trio. Their first performance with Skiba on March 18, 2015, marked the first time Mark Hoppus played in Blink without Tom DeLonge, after which Skiba was made an official member. "Mark and Travis had no plans to kill Blink so they brought in Matt Skiba from Alkaline Trio."

xref.title: Max Schieber Joins (2015)
xref.body: In March 2015, following Tom Delonge's second departure, Blink-182 played two club shows with Max Schieber (likely Matt Skiba) of Alkaline Trio filling in as guitarist. Lawyers worked to formalize Tom's exit and Max's integration into the band. "In March 2015, Blink played two club shows without Tom. Max Schieber, the guitarist for a band called Alkaline Trio filled in."

xref.title: Graceful Departure from Blink 182 (2022)
xref.body: Upon the announcement of Tom DeLonge's return to Blink 182, Matt Skiba handled the situation "like a pro." He was aware the announcement was forthcoming, accepted the circumstances gracefully, and extended his congratulations and thanks to the band members for the opportunity he had been given. "Matskiba took it like a pro. He knew the announcement was coming. He accepted the situation gracefully and congratulated the guys and thanked them for the opportunity of being in the band."

xref.title: Tom DeLonge's Return and Reconciliation (2022)
xref.body: By mid-2022, rumors of a reunion circulated, leading to the band's social media accounts being wiped in October. On October 11, the official announcement was made that Tom DeLonge was back, and an album and a two-year world tour were planned. This reconciliation was spurred by Mark Hoppus's cancer diagnosis, which prompted Tom to reach out immediately. "And that's when news came down that Mark, Travis and Tom, came to the realization that it was time to bury all the animosities and get back to being Blink 182."

xref.title: Dislike of Reality TV Presence
xref.body: Tom Delonge expressed his disapproval of Travis Barker's involvement in reality television, specifically the MTV show "Meet the Barkers," which extensively documented Travis and his wife Shannon Mochler. The presence of TV cameras, even in the Blink-182 rehearsal space, was a source of discomfort for Tom. "Tom also wasn't a fan of Travis getting into the reality TV show game."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Entrepreneurial Ventures
xref.body: Outside of music, Tom DeLonge founded a shoe company called McBeth, which achieved success. He also established a software company named Mod Life, specifically designed to help musicians monetize their creative output. These ventures reflected his diverse interests beyond performance. "Plus, he had a shoe company called McBeth that was doing well. Then there was his software company called Mod Life, which is aimed at helping musicians monetize what they produced."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Filling In for Tom DeLonge
xref.body: In March 2015, Max Schieber (guitarist for Alkaline Trio) stepped in to play with Blink-182 for two club shows following Tom DeLonge's second departure. Lawyers subsequently worked to formalize Tom's exit and Max's position within the band. "Max Schieber, the guitarist for a band called Alkaline Trio filled in."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Financial Security
xref.body: Tom DeLonge possesses substantial financial resources, which contribute to his overall satisfaction and independence. Being part of a band that sold approximately 40 million albums means that monetary concerns are largely irrelevant for him. "He has more than enough money to keep him happy. And when you're in a band that sold 40 million or so albums, you know, money's not much of a problem."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Five-Year Silence with Tom DeLonge
xref.body: By mid-2008, a significant communication breakdown had occurred between Travis Barker and Tom DeLonge, with Travis noting that he hadn't spoken a word to Tom in five years. This extended silence highlighted the deep rifts within Blink-182, making the prospect of a reunion seem unlikely. "Travis hadn't said a word to Tom in five years or would be the point of getting back together of nobody's talking."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Formation and Personal Struggles
xref.body: Angels & Airwaves was formed by Tom DeLonge during Blink-182's hiatus. This period was marked by personal struggles for Tom, including a nervous breakdown attributed to the Blink-182 breakup, a severe back condition, and addiction to painkillers, which affected his clarity of thought. He dedicated months to working on new material in his home studio, teaching himself piano and audio engineering, finding the process therapeutic. "Tom was completely invisible the entire time, Plus 44 was in the news. The breakup of Blink caused what he'd later call a nervous breakdown."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Literary Ambitions
xref.body: Tom DeLonge has expanded his creative endeavors into writing, undertaking ambitious projects such as writing up to 15 novels. Each novel is co-authored with different individuals and is conceived to be accompanied by its own album, creating an interconnected multimedia universe. "he had all kinds of other things he wanted to do, including running up to 15 novels, each with different co-authors, each with albums to go with them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Lost Time Periods Near Area 51
xref.body: While researching Area 51, Tom DeLonge claims to have endured "lost time periods" during which he cannot remember what happened. This occurred when he was camping near Groom Lake in Nevada, where he had some kind of encounter, and next thing he knew, three hours had passed without his recollection. "He was camping out near Groom Lake in Nevada when he had some kind of encounter Next thing he knows three hours had gone by and he has no idea what happened during those three hours"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Even More Rock Conspiracies

xref.title: Majestic 12 Contact Claim
xref.body: Tom DeLonge claims that members of the modern-day Majestic 12, a group of scientists and military types prominent in UFO lore who know about UFOs, have been in contact with him. "Tom claims that members of the modern-day majestic 12 have been in touch with him"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Even More Rock Conspiracies

xref.title: Mark Hoppus's Isolation During Side Projects
xref.body: While Tom DeLonge and Travis Barker pursued side projects like Box Car Racer and The Transplants, Mark Hoppus "stayed on the sidelines quietly fuming," feeling betrayed that Tom had asked Travis to drum for Box Car Racer, a project that had an "old DIY vibe of early Blink." "Mark left the studio and wrote what he thought would be an instant rejection."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

xref.title: Moon Landing Stance
xref.body: Tom DeLonge believes that man landed on the moon, asserting that any theories to the contrary (like Stanley Kubrick faking it) are distractions from the "real thing," which is that something was found on the moon that humanity is not meant to know about. "He does believe the man landed on the moon anything to the contrary like I said Stanley Kubrick faked it on a soundstage someplace Has been leaked to distract us from the real thing which is We found something on the moon and we just can't let humanity know about it. We must keep it secret"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Even More Rock Conspiracies

xref.title: Origin and Purpose
xref.body: Box Car Racer was Tom DeLonge's project, driven by his need to play more aggressive punk music and to occupy himself while recovering from back surgery. He did not envision it as a permanent band. "This was Tom's product and his chance to exercise his need to play punk that was dirtier and more aggressive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

xref.title: Partial Catalog Sale
xref.body: Tom DeLonge sold just a portion of his song catalog. "It's like corn, tom de long, Dave Navarro and many others have sold just a portion of their portfolio of songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Buying Catalogues - A Primer

xref.title: Personal Hardships (2000s)
xref.body: During the mid-2000s, Tom DeLonge faced significant personal challenges. His brother was deployed to Iraq, a war he opposed, and his father was diagnosed with leukemia. These events, combined with the Blink-182 breakup and a serious back injury that led to painkiller addiction, created a difficult period in his life. "His brother was deployed to Iraq, a war that Tom opposed. His father was diagnosed with leukemia. In other words, it wasn't a very good time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Phone Tapping Suspicions
xref.body: Tom DeLonge is convinced that the CIA or some other entity once tapped his phone to discover what he knows, possibly related to "zero point energy," which is prominent in UFO investigations. "He is sure that the CIA or someone once tapped his phone to find out what he knows Maybe it's about zero point energy"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Even More Rock Conspiracies

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Political Activism
xref.body: Tom DeLonge became actively involved in politics, endorsing John Kerry for president and campaigning on the election circuit for a period. His political engagement stemmed from a desire for reform after four years of George Bush's presidency, deeply influencing the philosophical underpinnings of his band, Angels & Airwaves. "He endorsed John Kerry for president. He got sucked into politics. He even toured the election circuit for a while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Political and Utopian Philosophy
xref.body: Angels & Airwaves' philosophy was deeply influenced by Tom DeLonge's engagement with politics, sparked by his endorsement of John Kerry for president and his opposition to the Iraq War (where his brother was deployed), alongside his father's leukemia diagnosis. The band adopted a strong streak of utopianism and positivity, with their motto being "Friends and Family First, Band Seconds," reflecting Tom's personal priorities. "Tom became committed to the idea of reform, and the work it would take to make this a better world. And this became baked into the philosophy of this band, Angels, and Airwaves."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Post-Blink-182 UFO Research Career
xref.body: After leaving Blink-182, Tom DeLonge embarked on a full-time career as a UFO researcher. He is dedicated to uncovering and exposing what he believes is a vast government conspiracy covering up the existence of aliens. "Tom DeLong isn't in Blink 1.2 anymore. He's working full-time as a UFO researcher and is determined to expose the vast government cover-up conspiracy of the existence of aliens."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind-Blowing Facts About Music in 60 Minutes: 2017 Edition

xref.title: Post-Take Off Your Pants and Jacket Break
xref.body: After fulfilling obligations for "Take Off Your Pants and Jacket," the band desperately needed a break due to intense pressure and internal tensions. Tom DeLonge also had serious back issues, including a herniated disc requiring surgery, necessitating time off from Blink 182. "They desperately needed some time apart."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

xref.title: Prolific Multimedia Output
xref.body: Since his departure from Blink-182, Tom DeLonge has been highly productive, releasing seven Angels & Airwaves projects, many of which are integral parts of larger multimedia endeavors. These include albums accompanied by animated films, EPs linked to novels co-authored by him, and concepts that extend into documentary series, demonstrating his broad creative scope. "There are now seven angels and airwaves releases."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Reality TV Show
xref.body: Travis Barker starred in a reality television series called "Meet the Barkers" on MTV. The show documented his life with his wife, Shannon Mochler, even extending to filming inside the Blink-182 rehearsal space, which was a point of contention for Tom DeLonge. "Remember, meet the Barkers? That was an MTV show that followed Travis and his wife Shannon Mochler everywhere, including into the Blink rehearsal space."

xref.title: Secret Alien Life Form Discovery Claim
xref.body: Tom DeLonge claims that an alien life form has already been discovered but is being kept secret from the public. "He claims that an alien life form has already been discovered but is being kept secret"

xref.title: To The Stars Academy Founding
xref.body: Tom DeLonge founded "To The Stars Academy," an organization described as "pretty serious," staffed with scientists, engineers, and military personnel who are all committed to understanding unidentified aerial phenomena. "He found it the to the stars Academy Which is a pretty serious organization stock with scientists engineers and military types who all want to believe"

xref.title: Tom Delonge's Desire for Break
xref.body: Tom Delonge's decision to take a break stemmed from feeling the intense grind of the band's schedule and needing at least six months to decompress. He was disappointed that Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker didn't fully understand his need for this extended time away. "The story seems to be that Tom just wanted a break from the grind and he was disappointed that the other two guys didn't understand why he needed at least six months to decompress."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Travis Barker's Involvement
xref.body: Travis Barker joined Tom DeLonge on drums for Box Car Racer, a decision that deeply upset Mark Hoppus of Blink 182, who felt betrayed. Travis only sang on a couple of tracks. "But then he asked Travis to be his drummer, which was okay for Travis, but it greatly pissed off Mark."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

xref.title: UFO Research Obsession
xref.body: Tom DeLonge is deeply obsessed with UFOs. His passion was so significant that it was a primary reason he quit blink-182, choosing to pursue UFO research full-time. "In fact, part of the reason he quit the band was so he could pursue this full time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Hobbies of Musicians

xref.title: Unfulfilled Movie Promise
xref.body: Following the release of their debut album, Tom DeLonge expressed significant satisfaction with Angels & Airwaves' initial output and promised fans a "mind blowing full length movie" in addition to new music. However, this full-length film project never materialized. "he promised that in addition to more new music there would be some kind of mind blowing full length movie. We never saw the movie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
